body.input:
Customer support call about: Locked out after a password reset
EMPLOYEE is Marcus Bell, the support employee being assessed. CUSTOMER is Priya Natarajan.
This is the complete call.

[turn-1] EMPLOYEE: Thanks for calling Contoso support, this is Marcus. How can I help today?
[turn-2] CUSTOMER: I reset my password an hour ago and now it says my account is locked. I've got a client presentation in twenty minutes and everything is in there.
[turn-3] EMPLOYEE: That's a stressful spot with a presentation so close, so let's move quickly. To make sure I'm talking to the account holder, can you confirm the email on the account and the code I've just sent to your phone?
[turn-4] CUSTOMER: It's priya.n@example.com, and the code is 482 913.
[turn-5] EMPLOYEE: Thank you, you're verified. Three failed sign-ins after the reset triggered the lock. I've cleared it now; please sign in with the new password while I stay on the line.
[turn-6] CUSTOMER: I'm in. Thank you, that was quick.

s_0.instructions: Rate the EMPLOYEE on "Empathy & active listening": Recognises how the customer feels and responds to what they actually said. Judge only what the transcript shows. Choose the level whose description fits best.
criteria: Dismissive: Ignores or contradicts what the customer said; shows no recognition of how they feel.
Minimal: A token acknowledgement, then straight back to script; the customer has to repeat themselves.
Adequate: Polite and responsive, but the acknowledgement is generic and the problem is not played back.
Strong: Names the customer's situation or feeling specifically and responds to what they actually said.
Exceptional: Consistently reflects the customer's words and priorities, repairs any misstep, and leaves them feeling heard.

o_0.instructions: Did this call give the EMPLOYEE a real opportunity to show "Empathy & active listening" (Recognises how the customer feels and responds to what they actually said.)? Answer no only if nothing in the call called for this skill.

s_1.instructions: Rate the EMPLOYEE on "Accuracy & honesty": Gives correct, consistent information and is honest about what is uncertain or outside their control. Judge only what the transcript shows. Choose the level whose description fits best.
criteria: Misleading: Gives wrong information or guarantees that the call shows to be false, and does not correct them.
Unreliable: Several unsupported claims or contradictions; corrections come only when the customer pushes.
Mostly accurate: Generally correct, with one notable unsupported claim or a gap the customer has to probe.
Accurate: Information is correct and consistent; limits and uncertainty are stated when asked.
Precise: Correct, consistent, and proactively clear about what is known, unknown and outside the employee's control.

o_1.instructions: Did this call give the EMPLOYEE a real opportunity to show "Accuracy & honesty" (Gives correct, consistent information and is honest about what is uncertain or outside their control.)? Answer no only if nothing in the call called for this skill.

s_2.instructions: Rate the EMPLOYEE on "Security & verification": Verifies identity before touching the account and refuses to bend that rule. Judge only what the transcript shows. Choose the level whose description fits best.
criteria: Breach: Changes or exposes account access or personal details with no identity verification.
Risky: Offers to skip verification, or verifies only after acting on the account.
Partial: Verifies, but incompletely or inconsistently across the call.
Sound: Verifies identity before accessing or changing the account.
Exemplary: Verifies before acting, explains why, and protects the account when asked to bend the rules.

o_2.instructions: Did this call give the EMPLOYEE a real opportunity to show "Security & verification" (Verifies identity before touching the account and refuses to bend that rule.)? Answer no only if nothing in the call called for this skill.

s_3.instructions: Rate the EMPLOYEE on "Resolution & ownership": Moves the issue to a clear resolution or a specific, owned next step. Judge only what the transcript shows. Choose the level whose description fits best.
criteria: Unresolved: No fix and no plan; the customer is left where they started.
Weak next step: A vague or unowned follow-up with no timeframe.
Partial: Some progress, but part of the issue is still open or unowned.
Resolved: The issue is fixed, or has a specific next step with an owner and a timeframe.
Resolved and proactive: Fixed and confirmed with the customer, with future problems anticipated and prevented.

o_3.instructions: Did this call give the EMPLOYEE a real opportunity to show "Resolution & ownership" (Moves the issue to a clear resolution or a specific, owned next step.)? Answer no only if nothing in the call called for this skill.

s_4.instructions: Rate the EMPLOYEE on "Clear communication": Uses plain language, confirms the details that matter and closes with a summary. Judge only what the transcript shows. Choose the level whose description fits best.
criteria: Confusing: The customer cannot tell what is happening or what to do.
Often unclear: Jargon, missing steps or contradictions force the customer to ask again.
Understandable: The customer can follow, but key details are not confirmed.
Clear: Plain language, one step at a time, with key details confirmed.
Exceptionally clear: Explains the why as well as the what, confirms details back, and closes with a summary.

o_4.instructions: Did this call give the EMPLOYEE a real opportunity to show "Clear communication" (Uses plain language, confirms the details that matter and closes with a summary.)? Answer no only if nothing in the call called for this skill.

risk.instructions: If the call ended right now, how likely is the CUSTOMER to escalate, complain, or stop using the company?
criteria: Low: the customer is satisfied or calmly working with the employee
Guarded: some frustration or doubt, but still engaged
Elevated: clear dissatisfaction, repeated pushback, or loss of trust
High: asks for a supervisor, threatens to complain or cancel, or has given up on the employee
